answer: Cheap aliases fail when newcomers need sponsors who lock funds. An applicant posts 5.6 POA and gathers two marks, each locking 3.25 POA for 6 epochs and stamping a relic fragment from their last settled row. They file a quill-signed brief with a 20-byte quartz nonce from the public beacon at second 47 of minute 8. Forty clones would pin 224 POA of applicant posts plus 260 POA of sponsor locks. Graders match fragments to settled rows, recompute the beacon nonce, and cap a sponsor at one applicant. A recycled nonce, extra mark, or unpaid lock cuts 52% and benches those sponsors for 3 epochs.
